help.tactics.even.bigGap: Big CA gap (Nordstern start): tactics help you steal points and avoid bad plans; they don’t make you favorites.
help.tactics.even.chess: It still won’t feel like “chess every week” unless we tune further; the underdog study shows tactics as marginal gains and damage control, not overturning a big numbers disadvantage.
help.tactics.even.evenQuality: When quality is even, the quality gap stops dominating, so the same tactical edge should matter more in percentage points.
help.tactics.even.hypothesis: Even teams (hypothesis, not yet studied): the same system should tip scales more often — roughly “regularly” in the sense of meaningful win/draw swing, not “win every time with the right slider.”
help.tactics.even.measured: What we measured: Nordstern (underdog) vs three league opponents, 375 plans × 20 runs each. On the same squad, best vs among-worst in the published top-10 band was on the order of ~0.3–0.5 goals per game average goal difference and large swings in win% on small samples.
help.tactics.even.notMeasured: What we did not measure: two teams with matched CA and the same lattice.
help.tactics.even.title: Do tactics tip the scales when teams are even?
help.tactics.how.formation.body: Changing formation reloads a full default plan for that shape: mentality, pressing, line height, width, tempo, intensity, fluidity, marking, and role duties (inverted full-backs vs overlapping, false nine vs poacher, etc.). Slots are re-filled for the new shape.
help.tactics.how.formation.title: Formation (4-3-3, 4-4-2, 2-3-5)
help.tactics.how.hidden.body: Everything else in the plan (width, tempo, intensity, fluidity, marking, keeper/fullback/wide/striker duties) rides along from the formation default unless you change formation. Career UI does not expose those extra knobs yet.
help.tactics.how.lede: Tactics are a SandboxPlan: everything the match wrapper passes into the engine on top of your XI + bench. Career matches use buildMatchView with squads built via applySandboxPlan — the engine itself is unchanged.
help.tactics.how.presets.body: Three style presets per save (Ballbesitz / Kompakt / Offensiv → default 4-3-3 / 4-4-2 / 2-3-5). Tapping a preset does not change formation; it only copies mentality, pressing, and line height from that preset’s saved plan onto your current formation. You can save the current sliders into a preset slot.
help.tactics.how.presets.title: Three style presets
help.tactics.how.sliders.readout: The Men / Prs / Lin line on the tactics card is your quick readout.
help.tactics.how.sliders.title: Fine tuning
help.tactics.how.title: How our tactics system works
help.tactics.opponents.body: AI clubs get a formation from club identity (e.g. traditional/workers → 4-4-2, others often 4-3-3) and fixed-ish sliders from world templates. Identity tweaks mentality/tempo/marking; there is no hidden match bonus for being “ambitious.”
help.tactics.opponents.title: What opponents do
help.tactics.playWell.away: Away vs clearly stronger CA: lean Kompakt (lower line/press → often low_block tag) or 4-4-2 — fewer open games; bad plans were often aggressive 2-3-5 with high press/line.
help.tactics.playWell.chase: Must chase a result: Offensiv 2-3-5 with eyes open — more variance; can improve attack or worsen goals against depending on opponent.
help.tactics.playWell.default: Default week, no scout: 4-3-3 preset Ballbesitz (~M58 P64 L56) — matches default preset 1; possession-ish duties; not crazy high line.
help.tactics.playWell.expect: Align expectations with design: Nordstern starts ~8–15 CA below the league median; underdog is start conflict, not permanent victimhood. Relegation is allowed; growth and transfers are the long arc.
help.tactics.playWell.lede: There is no universal best tactic; offline research on the same XI already shows different top plans per opponent on early matchdays. Still, a sensible playbook:
help.tactics.playWell.lineup: Lineup still beats sliders: weak CAs in wrong roles matter more than +6 on pressing. Tactics are the marginal layer on top of personnel.
help.tactics.playWell.scout: Scout report available: prefer the recommended formation + risk row that matches your risk tolerance — only 10 sims, but they’re tied to your presets and current plan.
help.tactics.playWell.study: Study hint (early Nordstern): often high line (L72) and mid–high press in top lattice cells — underdog games stayed low-scoring; high line sometimes helped goal diff, not 70% wins.
help.tactics.playWell.title: If you want to play well as Nordstern
help.tactics.recap.item1: Explain tactics: formation + hidden duty package + three sliders you tune; three savable presets; engine reads full plan.
help.tactics.recap.item2: Play well: scout when you can, don’t blindly max press/line as Nordstern, match risk to home/away and table situation; formation change is a big reset — use it deliberately.
help.tactics.recap.item3: Bad team / relegation / growth arc: aligned with design; tactics are part of “hold on while the squad grows,” not a day-one cheat code.
help.tactics.recap.item4: Even teams: plausible that tactics tip outcomes more often than for Nordstern; current numbers are underdog-only and support modest edges, not dominance.
help.tactics.recap.title: Short recap
help.tactics.scout.body: When the scout job finishes, 10 headless sims run with the same squads as the real fixture; only your plan varies: sim 0 = your current plan, then cycles your three presets’ plans. The Postfach card aggregates scorelines, a 4×3 grid, and 2–3 formation/risk rows — not the full 375-point lattice (that’s offline research only).
help.tactics.scout.risk: Risk tags are coarse: high line (line ≥ 62 and press ≥ 58), low block (line ≤ 45 and press ≤ 48), else balanced.
